# Scope

This document verifies execution of the source-locked evidence-audit
functions on a deliberately **synthetic** fragmented trajectory dataset.
It is not a biological validation, a detector benchmark, a physical
underwater reconstruction or a causal treatment evaluation.

# Complete executable workflow

The example constructs source observations, compares pooled and
time-window-balanced estimators, verifies a designed sign reversal,
audits measurement semantics and independent-unit support, calculates
spatial and measurement-geometry diagnostics, runs placebo cuts, and
exports a manifest-verified research report.

~~~{r complete-example, echo=TRUE, results='hold'}
example_file <- system.file("examples","evidence_guardrails.R",
                           package="aquaTrajectories")
stopifnot(nzchar(example_file),file.exists(example_file))
source(example_file,local=TRUE)
~~~

# Interpretation

The *positive pooled* and *negative time-balanced* results are
constructed from the known fixture to verify that the software
exposes analysis-specification sensitivity rather than concealing it.
All animal- and tank-level inference remains blocked by default.
Three source-variable axes can be visualized while physical 3D
calibration remains unverified.

# Reproducibility

The script creates its results in a fresh temporary directory, hashes
all emitted artifacts, confirms the manifest, and refuses to infer
independent animals from software track IDs.
